reasoning_content: Hmm, `ps` didn't show 5538/5539, but pgrep -f vite returned 5588 and 5589 (different PIDs—these might be new ones, or pgrep's pattern might be matching other things). Wait a minute—`pgrep -f vite` matches any process that contains "vite" in its command line. This might include the shell that's running my own pgrep command. Let me check what 5588/5589 actually are.

action.command: ps -o pid,ppid,cmd -p 5588,5589 2>/dev/null; echo "---"; ps aux | grep -iE "vite|node" | grep -v grep | head -10; echo "=== done ==="
